stemMd: Which finding would most strengthen the planners' mixed approach?

options.label: A
options.textMd: The island once had a different name.

options.label: B
options.textMd: The earliest survey is easier to copy than later records.

options.label: C
options.textMd: Residents disagree over the word authentic.

options.label: D
options.textMd: An old map uses an attractive color scheme.

options.label: E
options.textMd: Trials show that retaining some grassland protects scarce species while woodland expansion on suitable slopes reduces erosion.

explanationMd: The finding links different interventions to the plan's explicit goals. It supports the claim that a mixed future landscape can be justified by outcomes rather than by fidelity to one date.

distractorRationale.c: That illustrates the debate but does not establish ecological benefits.
distractorRationale.b: Convenience does not justify a restoration target.
distractorRationale.d: Cartographic appearance is irrelevant to ecological goals.
distractorRationale.a: Naming history does not assess the interventions.
